reports.notes: TYPED (machine-filled) form - the only non-handwritten filing among this filer's two in the chunk, and the figures are crisp; all values high confidence. OFFICE: the page's Office Seeking field reads 'Utah County Commissioner' with NO SEAT LETTER. office_index carries the more specific 'County Commission Seat C'. Per the corpus rule against inferring an unprinted seat, office_printed is exactly what the page says; the seat is not transcribed. (This filer's OTHER 2012 filing, key 9cceca7c, left Office Seeking entirely blank.) The summary page's own header boxes - Page/of, Candidate Last Name, Date of Report - were left EMPTY on this filing; report_date therefore comes from the cover's signature Date, 'July 19, 2012'. Line 3 (7,528.24) equals line 7 of this filer's 6-19-12 report, correctly carried forward. Clerk Date received is hand-written '7/20/12' with a note 'Express Mail'. AMENDMENT: 'No' is checked. candidate_index was blank; the page names Lorne W. Grierson.

contributions.detail: Schedule A (p3) is a wholly EMPTY printed grid — 17 underline rules, not one written entry in any of the four columns — and the filer typed 0.00 into BOTH of the schedule's own printed footer cells. Zero rows sum to 0.00, which equals the cover's promoted PER-PERIOD cell (Column A line 1 = 0.00) and equals line 4 'Total Contributions Received (From Line 1 Column A) = 0.00'. These are typed NUMERALS (0.00), not nil marks, so the zero-glyph question does not arise. Column B 'Year-to-Date Total' prints 13,212.30 and is NOT summed as an increment (utah is a per-period regime) — it carries this filer's earlier 2012 reports, which this report does not itemize. The p2 balance ladder closes on its own terms: line 3 7,528.24 + line 4 0.00 = line 5 7,528.24; 7,528.24 - line 6 5,360.11 = line 7 2,168.13 exactly.

itemized.notes: CLOSES THE 2012 CYCLE (8th of 8). Page-face candidate 'Lorne W. Grierson' (Republican, Orem) — index.csv names NO candidate for this row, so the page face supplies it; the page-face office reads 'Utah County Commissioner' with NO SEAT PRINTED, while the channel label says 'County Commission Seat C' — per the brief the seat is NOT inferred from the filing, and the divergence is recorded here rather than adjudicated. 4 pages: p1 cover (Type of Report ticked '30 Days after the Primary Election', amendment 'No' ticked, signed and dated July 19, 2012, clerk's 'Date received 7/20/12' stamp with 'Express Mail'); p2 SUMMARY PAGE (located by its printed heading, which happens to be p2 as usual for legacy_colAB); p3 SCHEDULE A 'ITEMIZED CONTRIBUTIONS RECEIVED'; p4 SCHEDULE B 'ITEMIZED EXPENDITURES MADE'. THIS FILING IS TYPED (machine-filled), unusual for the era and unusually clean to read — but it is still a scan, so row confidence stays 'medium' per SCHEMA §6. SCHEDULE A IS AN EMPTY-SCHEDULE, not a withheld side and not a no-schedule-page: the page exists, its printed grid carries no entry at all, and the filer typed 0.00 into both the 'Subtotal for this page' and 'Total Contributions Received' cells, so the absence of donors this period is what the document itself states. CONFIRMS ADDENDUM B §B4 on the 2012 form: underline grid, 17 printed rules, four columns, text above the rule, three printed anchors per side, and Schedule B reusing Schedule A's headings so `purpose` is honestly blank. FOLIATION: a FOURTH 2012 practice — the 'Page __ of __', 'Candidate or Officeholder's Last Name' and 'Date of Report' boxes are printed on p2, p3 and p4 and this filer left ALL of them completely BLANK, so the filing foliates itself not at all (companion to B4's three practices). PRIVACY: Schedule B's 'Mailing Address & Zip Code' column carries full street lines for all 7 vendors; expenditure rows carry no address field by contract and NOTHING from that column has been reproduced here, not even a zip. NOTE ON THE SIBLING FILING: the same filer's other 2012 report (key 9cceca7c) is where the 'LOAN TO SELF' contribution question was decided (ADDENDUM B §B3); no loan line appears on this filing, whose only ledger is the expenditure side.
